item.title: Statement by Premier Lantz on the suspension of Canada-U.S. trade discussions and implementation of new U.S. tariffs
item.description:
Statement by Premier Lantz on the suspension of Canada-U.S. trade discussions and implementation of new U.S. tariffs jpranahan Sun, 08/23/2026 - 11:48

Hon. Rob Lantz, Premier of Prince Edward Island, issued the following statement following the suspension of trade discussions between Canada and the United States and the implementation of new U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods:

“The breakdown of the Canada-U.S. trade negotiations was not the news any of us wanted to hear. I know this was a difficult decision for Prime Minister Carney, but I want to be very clear: it was absolutely the right one for our country.

Canada went to the table looking for a fair deal. But there are some things we should never be willing to trade away simply for the sake of reaching an agreement. We will never accept terms that undermine Canadian industry, Canadian workers or our national sovereignty.

These are unjustified tariffs being imposed by the United States, and the unfortunate reality is they will have real and direct impacts on businesses, workers and families here in Prince Edward Island and across Canada.

I want to thank Prime Minister Carney, Minister Dominic LeBlanc, Chief Negotiator Janice Charette and the entire Canadian negotiating team for their leadership and close collaboration with First Ministers throughout these negotiations.

Here at home, our job now is to stand with Island workers, businesses and families, and make sure our province is ready for what comes next. Our government is immediately convening Cabinet and the Cabinet Committee on Trade Relations to assess what these latest U.S. trade actions mean for Prince Edward Island.

We will review the supports already in place for businesses and workers and make adjustments where they are needed. We will continue to support the industries that are the backbone of our economy, help Island businesses diversify their markets, and pursue strategic investments that strengthen our economy for the long term.

Because our response cannot only be about getting through the days and weeks ahead. It also has to be about building a stronger Island economy for the future.

We cannot control the decisions being made in Washington. But we can control how we respond here at home, and every Islander has a part to play.

When you have the choice, buy local and buy Canadian. Every dollar spent on an Island or Canadian product supports the worker who made it, the farmer who grew it, the fisher who caught it, the producer who processed it and the business that put it on the shelf. Where we spend our hard-earned money matters. Those choices add up.

There is uncertainty ahead, and we should be honest about that. But Islanders know how to meet difficult moments. We pull together. We look out for one another. And when something matters, we stand up for it.

That is what Canada is doing now, and it is what our government will continue to do for our province. We will stand up for our businesses. We will stand up for our workers. And we will make sure Islanders have the support they need in the days ahead.

There will be challenges, but I have every confidence in our province and in the people who call it home. We will get through this, and we will do it together.”

item.title: PEI offering free hunting licences to Canadian Armed Forces Veterans and active members of the Canadian Forces
item.description:
PEI offering free hunting licences to Canadian Armed Forces Veterans and active members of the Canadian Forces jpranahan Thu, 08/20/2026 - 14:03

Beginning this hunting season, Canadian Armed Forces Veterans and active members of the Canadian Forces can receive a free hunting licence.   

“Hunting is enjoyed by residents and visitors to the Island, with more than 2,500 licences sold annually, and time spent outdoors is good for our mental and physical health. In addition to free angling licences for Veterans and active members of the Canadian Forces introduced in 2024, adding free hunting licences is just a small token of appreciation for those who have served our country.”

- Land and Environment Minister Darlene Compton

Duck and goose populations are healthy, thanks in part to decades of conservation efforts, both here in PEI and throughout North America.

Registration is now open for the 2026 Provincial Hunting Workshop which will take place on Saturday, September 12 from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m.  Participants (ages 12 and up) will rotate through stations learning about firearm safety, wildlife conservation, hunting regulations and enforcement, map and compass use, skeet shooting and waterfowl hunting techniques. 

Participants who complete this free workshop, along with the online portion of the Hunter Safety Course, receive hunter certification and a PEI Wildlife card as well as a free 2026-2027 hunting licence and conservation fee. Register online at Hunting, Firearms, and Bow Hunting Safety Courses. Individuals who are unable to register online can call Forests, Fish and Wildlife at (902) 368-4683 to complete their registration by phone.

Hunting licences, including courtesy licences for Veterans and active members of the Canadian Forces, will be available August 25 online at Buy a Hunting Licence Online and at local retailers.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
